title: Rest in God above all (III.21)
hook: above all goods and gifts, rest in God
tomorrow: what do you do when the map says no route found?

segments.voice: Yesterday, four loosened grips: another's will, less, the lower place, God's will. The line was four things.

Health, a good friend, a scholarship, a knee that works again. If God's gifts are good, why rest above them? That's a real question, and two Catholic voices answer it differently. In chapter twenty-one of book three, the Imitation's disciple empties a whole bag of good things onto the table and asks to rest above every one of them. Another Catholic voice, older still in its roots, says something that sounds like the opposite.
screen: `IF THE GIFTS ARE GOOD…` → `WHY REST ABOVE THEM?` → `TWO CATHOLIC VOICES.`

segments.voice: The first voice is the Imitation. Above all things and in all things, the soul tells itself, rest in the Lord. The Latin begins super omnia, above all. Then the list: above health and beauty, glory and honor, power, knowledge, riches, joy, fame, comfort, hope. Above every gift God can give, and above everything that is not God. Its reason: whatever God gives apart from himself is too small to satisfy the heart. Its best case is simple. Gifts can be lost, and a heart that rests only in them has nowhere to stand when they go. The second voice starts in Genesis, in the Douay-Rheims: "And God saw all the things that he had made, and they were very good." Thomas Aquinas built on that, teaching that grace doesn't destroy nature but brings it to its fullness. Its best case: the gifts are how God's goodness reaches you. Look away from the sunset and the friend to find God, and you may miss where God is showing up. Here's what to tell someone tonight: the Imitation never calls the gifts bad. It calls them too small to lie down in. And the Church keeps both voices on its shelf, the book that rests above the gifts and the teacher who loves them.
screen: `SUPER OMNIA: ABOVE ALL.` · `GIFTS CAN BE LOST.` · `AND THEY WERE VERY GOOD.` · `GRACE BRINGS NATURE TO FULLNESS.` · then, large: `REST ABOVE ALL.`

segments.voice: Count three good things you have right now, one finger at a time, and thank God for each, or simply be glad of it. Then open your hand and let all three rest on your palm without closing around them. Stay there, holding them lightly.
Rest in God above all. The Imitation's call to rest above every good gift, because the Giver is the only place big enough to lie down.
screen: `REST IN GOD ABOVE ALL — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: rest above all. The gifts stay good; they just aren't the bed. Sleep well.

howItsDone: Catholics thank God for good things in grace before meals and at night prayer, and many spiritual writers, the Imitation among them, also urge resting the heart in God himself rather than in any gift.

fork.setup: your friend loves hiking and says it's where she feels closest to God. a classmate quotes the Imitation: rest above every creature. what's the Imitation side's best case to her?
options: the mountain can be lost; a heart resting only there has nowhere to stand.
nature is a distraction, so she should pray indoors instead.
feeling close to God outdoors is only a mood, not prayer.
fork.reveal: the Imitation never calls the gifts bad. its best case: gifts pass, so rest in the Giver. and her side has Genesis and Aquinas: the gifts are very good.

original.note: Latin, Imitation III.21: above all, the chapter's first words for where to rest.

what a scholar hears: two strands kept side by side, the Imitation's 'above all' and Aquinas's 'grace perfects nature' (Summa Theologiae I, q. 1, a. 8).

chat.says: let daniela drive. but i pray for abuela's knee like 50x a day. is wanting the gift that much wrong?
options: Not wrong. The knee is a good gift; the Imitation just says rest in the Giver, not the gift.
Kind of. The Imitation says want nothing but God, so stop asking for the knee.
No. The knee's what matters right now; God can wait until she's better.
chat.meaning: The Imitation never calls gifts bad, only too small to rest in. Genesis calls them very good. Ask for the gift; rest in God.
